stable.label: iOS 27
stable.notes: Major release introducing Siri AI, performance improvements, and parental controls. Compatible with iPhone 11 and later.

upcomingFeature.label: iOS 27.1
upcomingFeature.notes: Expected language expansions and polish. Check Settings > General > Software Update.

beta.label: iOS 27.2 (beta)
beta.notes: Developer beta. Not for daily drivers.

communitySentiment.label: Mostly positive after first week
communitySentiment.summary: Launch-week reports largely quieted. Temporary battery/indexing hit is normal. Siri AI strong on supported chips.
communitySentiment.sourceNote: Synthesized from Apple Newsroom, MacRumors, Reddit r/ios, and tech press (as of 28 Sep 2026).

updateProbability.label: Reasonably safe to update for most users

breakdown.note: Recommend on A16+; wait on older chips.
First week of major iOS is riskiest.

adviceByTier.ai: High confidence — update now if you want Siri AI.
adviceByTier.mid: Good confidence — safe for most; short wait only if battery is critical.
adviceByTier.entry: Moderate — security fixes yes; older chips feel early slowdowns more. Prefer 27.0.1 / 27.1.

ios.pointReleaseAdvice: Major .0 releases carry the highest early risk. Point releases are lower risk. Waiting 7–14 days on older hardware is reasonable.
ios.lede: Pick your iPhone. We'll compare the latest iOS release against your device, factor in known post-launch issues, and tell you whether to update now, wait, or skip.

stable.label: Android 17
stable.notes: Stable release with App Bubbles, stronger Live Threat Detection, Mark as Lost improvements, large-screen adaptive requirements, and productivity features. Rolling out to Pixel 6+ first, then OEM skins (One UI 9, etc.) through late 2026.

upcomingFeature.label: Android 17 QPR1
upcomingFeature.notes: Quarterly Platform Release — bug fixes, security patches, and feature polish. Pixel typically first; OEM timing varies.

beta.label: Android 18 (preview)
beta.notes: Next major version in early developer testing when available. Not for primary devices.

communitySentiment.label: Stable on Pixel; OEM rollouts ongoing
communitySentiment.summary: Android 17 is mature on supported Pixels (since June 2026). Samsung One UI 9 and other OEM skins are rolling out in waves — early OEM builds can lag Pixel stability by weeks. Security patches matter more than the major version alone on Android.
communitySentiment.sourceNote: Synthesized from Android Developers Blog, Android Central, 9to5Google, Reddit r/Android, and OEM release notes (as of 28 Sep 2026).

updateProbability.label: Safe on Pixel / recent flagships; wait for your OEM if early

breakdown.note: One UI 9 started mid-September; phased by model.
Generally positive on Pixel; mixed on first OEM builds.
Staying current on security patches is the main win.
First OEM drops sometimes need a hotfix week.

adviceByTier.flagship: Update when your OEM offers it — flagships get the most testing.
adviceByTier.mid: Good to update for security; if the build is brand-new from your OEM, waiting 3–7 days is fine.
adviceByTier.budget: Prioritize the latest security patch. Major version is secondary if your OEM is slow.

android.pointReleaseAdvice: On Android, monthly security patches often matter more than jumping to the newest major version immediately. After a major OEM skin update, waiting a few days for hotfix reports is sensible.
